This page covers installing thipR and connecting to THIP. The guides that follow
form a short course; they run on an invented example database, so you can follow
along before you have THIP access.

| Guide | What you will learn |
|---|---|
| [Meet the THIP data](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/meet-the-data.html) | The yearly tables, what one row is, the main columns |
| [Working with a database from R](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/database-from-r.html) | Where your code runs, and when data come into R |
| [From question to cohort](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/question-to-cohort.html) | Turn a research question into one entry per person |
| [Look back and follow up](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/look-back-follow-up.html) | Fetch each person's history and outcomes around their entry |
| [Flag conditions](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/condition-flags.html) | Turn reviewed code lists into flags per person or entry |
| [Worked example](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/getting-started.html) | The whole course in one short analysis |
| [Check before you trust](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/data-checks.html) | Checks to run on the data before relying on it |
| [Using THIP data responsibly](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/responsible-use.html) | Working habits: where records stay, small counts, credentials |

The code on this page is shown, not run: setting up and connecting work only
inside your THIP account, so run those steps there.

## Install or load thipR

> **Temporary setup guidance — update to come.** The ADBC backend is experimental.
> For now, run `thipR::thip_install_driver()` once after installing thipR.
> This function downloads and installs the driver for you. This extra command
> may become unnecessary when the platform supplies the driver. These
> instructions will be updated as the installation workflow is refined.

Install from GitHub in R. The required R dependencies install automatically:

```{r install-thip, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")  # Once, if needed
remotes::install_github("Songyosr/thipR")
thipR::thip_install_driver()  # Downloads and installs the database driver
library(thipR)
```

`thip_install_driver()` handles the driver download and installation; you do not
need to download or install the driver manually. It is an **interim setup step**
for platforms that do not yet supply the ClickHouse ADBC driver. It uses `dbc`
to download and install a prebuilt driver with signature verification. It needs
an existing `dbc` executable or Python 3 with venv and pip to set one up. It does not require the R arrow package or an Arrow C++ build.
The smaller R dependencies may still need standard compilation tools when
installed from source.

The default destination is `file.path(tools::R_user_dir("thipR", "data"), "adbc")`,
a user-data folder normally under your home directory. Re-running the helper
reuses a working driver without upgrading it. If the platform supplies a driver,
skip the helper. Its location follows the upstream
[dbc driver installation rules](https://docs.columnar.tech/dbc/guides/installing/)
when using a platform installation.

For a custom destination:

```{r driver-location, eval=FALSE}
thip_install_driver(path = "~/my-drivers")
# Use this folder explicitly in later sessions:
con <- thip_connect(backend = "adbc", driver = "~/my-drivers")
```

The helper is temporary as a setup workaround; the installed files are not
session-temporary. They survive only while the chosen folder is preserved.
Confirm persistent storage with your platform team, especially for server
rebuilds. The helper does not edit `.libPaths()`, `.Renviron` or `.Rprofile`;
R package library configuration is a separate platform concern.

The ADBC backend is experimental and selected with `backend = "adbc"` in setup
and connections. Setup checks for the driver before asking for credentials and
prints the installation command if it is missing; it never downloads drivers.
SELECT/WITH queries run immediately; prepared parameters are
not supported. Signed 64-bit integers are returned as text. Unsigned 64-bit
values at or above 2^53 raise an error; select `toString(column)` for exact values.
Use `thip_table()` date conversions (Date32/DateTime64); raw legacy ClickHouse
Date/DateTime fields may be returned as numbers by the driver.

The existing HTTP backend remains the default for compatibility. To use it,
install the optional dependency separately:

```{r optional-http, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("ClickHouseHTTP")  # May also install R arrow
con <- thip_connect(backend = "http")
```

Installing thipR does not grant THIP database access. Credentials come from the
platform. For a fixed release use `remotes::install_github("Songyosr/thipR@v0.3.0")`;
that older release uses ClickHouseHTTP and does not include the ADBC helper.

Restart an existing R kernel after upgrading an already-loaded package.
A source archive (`.tar.gz`) is another installation option; builds that include
vignettes support `vignette("start-here", package = "thipR")` locally. The course
guides are on the website.

## Configure once, connect each session

```{r configure, eval=FALSE}
library(thipR)
thip_setup(backend = "adbc")
```

Run this once, in a notebook cell inside your THIP account. You will see, in order:

1. **Two text prompts**: `Database host:` and then `Database username:`. Enter the
   values provided by the THIP team. Port `8123`, database `thip` and scheme
   `http` use their defaults and are not asked for.
2. **A masked password box**: `Database password:`. Typed characters show as dots.
3. **A short pause** while a read-only check connects and then disconnects.
4. **One confirmation line**: "THIP configuration saved with owner-only
   permissions and loaded in this session."

```
thip_setup(backend = "adbc")
#> Database host: <host provided by the THIP team>
#> Database username: <your database username>
#> Database password: (masked box)
#> THIP configuration saved with owner-only permissions and loaded in this session.
```

Setup saves six `THIP_DB_*` lines to your `~/.Renviron` with owner-only
permissions. In later sessions, call `thip_connect(backend = "adbc")` only. If the check fails,
nothing is saved and you can simply run `thip_setup(backend = "adbc")` again.

| Message or symptom | Meaning and what to do |
|---|---|
| "THIP configuration already exists" | Setup was done before. Use `thip_connect(backend = "adbc")`, or `thip_setup(backend = "adbc", overwrite = TRUE)` to replace the saved values. |
| "Cannot load the ClickHouse ADBC driver" | Run `thip_install_driver()` to download and install the driver, then retry setup. For a custom folder, pass the same `driver` argument to setup and connections. |
| "THIP connection verification failed" | The host, username or password is wrong, or the database is unreachable. Nothing was saved; run setup again. |
| "host must be a hostname without a URL, path or credentials" | Enter only the host name, without `http://`, a port or a path. |
| "Input unavailable or cancelled" | A prompt was cancelled or could not be shown. Run setup in an interactive notebook cell. |
| No masked password box outside Jupyter | In RStudio or a terminal, install the `askpass` package. |

The `.Renviron` file is protected by file permissions; it is **plaintext**, not
encrypted. If the platform already supplies the `THIP_DB_*` variables, skip setup.
Never type credentials into notebook code or commit them to a repository. A
Jupyter API token is not used by thipR.

```{r connect, eval=FALSE}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr)
con <- thip_connect(backend = "adbc")
thip_tables(con)
thip_columns(con, "nhso2568")
```

The connection can only read, and a query that passes the platform's limits on
time or rows stops with an error rather than returning part of the result;
[Working with a database from
R](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/database-from-r.html) shows where
your code runs and when data come into R.

## Finish a session

```{r disconnect, eval=FALSE}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Check the installation after restarting R

After disconnecting, restart R and run this small query without reinstalling
the package or running the driver helper. It does not read stored records:

```{r check-installation, eval=FALSE}
con <- thipR::thip_connect(backend = "adbc")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 1 AS ok")  # Expect one row: ok = 1
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

This checks reuse in a new R session. A full notebook server restart or rebuild
is a separate persistence test: the package library and driver folder both need
to remain available. For a custom driver folder, include
`driver = "~/my-drivers"` in each connection call.

Next: [Meet the THIP data](https://songyosr.github.io/thipR/articles/meet-the-data.html)
starts the course.
